dataset_metadata.name: Mining Safety Protocols Reference Dataset
dataset_metadata.description: Comprehensive real-world mining safety protocols, thresholds, regulations, and procedures for underground and surface operations

requirements.primary_ventilation: Surface-mounted main fans providing airflow to all active workings via intake and return airways. System must maintain positive pressure differential of minimum 25 Pa across mine seals.
requirements.auxiliary_ventilation: Forcing or exhausting fan systems with ducting to dead-end headings. Duct diameter minimum 600mm for headings up to 100m, 900mm for headings exceeding 100m.
requirements.fresh_air_supply: Minimum 0.3 m³/s per person underground at all times per MSHA 30 CFR 75.323.
requirements.diesel_air_quantity: Minimum 6 m³/s per kW of rated diesel engine power for equipment operating underground.
requirements.refuge_chamber_air: Minimum 0.5 m³/s fresh air supply to each permanently installed refuge chamber.
requirements.split_systems: Intake air must not pass through more than one working section before reaching surface. Return air from each working split must discharge directly to surface or main return.
requirements.air_velocity_minimum: 0.5 m/s minimum in active travelways, 1.0 m/s minimum in active working faces.
requirements.air_velocity_maximum: 5.0 m/s maximum in travelways to prevent dust re-entrainment, 7.0 m/s maximum in shafts.
requirements.temperature_underground: Wet bulb temperature must not exceed 27.5°C in active workings per MSHA guidelines. Where exceeded, engineering controls and work-rest cycles mandatory.
requirements.recirculation_prohibition: Air recirculation systems prohibited unless equipped with validated gas scrubbing and filtration achieving >99.9% contaminant removal, approved by regulatory authority.
requirements.monitoring_frequency: Continuous real-time monitoring at main fan stations, working faces, and return airways. Manual verification checks every 4 hours.
requirements.fan_failure_protocol: If main fan fails, all personnel must evacuate to fresh air intakes within 15 minutes. No re-entry until ventilation restored and air quality verified by certified mine examiner.

gases_to_monitor.name: Oxygen
gases_to_monitor.effects_at_low_levels: Impaired judgment at 16%, unconsciousness at 14%, death within minutes at 12%

gases_to_monitor.name: Methane
gases_to_monitor.normal_atmosphere: 0.0% in coal, trace in hard rock
gases_to_monitor.monitoring_equipment: Catalytic bead or infrared sensors, MSHA-approved personal monitors
gases_to_monitor.calibration_frequency: Weekly bump test, monthly full calibration

alarm_thresholds.second_action: 1.0% - Stop all electrical equipment except intrinsically safe, increase ventilation
alarm_thresholds.third_action: 1.5% - Withdraw all personnel from affected area
alarm_thresholds.evacuation: 2.0% - Immediate evacuation of mine, seal affected area

gases_to_monitor.notes: In coal mines, methane liberation rates must be assessed and ventilation designed for maximum anticipated emission rate plus 25% safety margin.

gases_to_monitor.name: Carbon Monoxide
gases_to_monitor.monitoring_equipment: Electrochemical sensors, infrared analyzers, Dräger tubes
gases_to_monitor.effects: Headache at 400 ppm, collapse at 800 ppm, death at 1500 ppm within minutes
gases_to_monitor.source_indicators: Spontaneous combustion, diesel exhaust, blasting fumes, underground fires
gases_to_monitor.smoke_detector_integration: CO monitoring integrated with fire detection systems; rising CO above baseline triggers investigation protocol

gases_to_monitor.name: Hydrogen Sulfide
gases_to_monitor.monitoring_equipment: Electrochemical sensors, lead acetate tape analyzers

alarm_thresholds.warning: 10 ppm - OSHA PEL TWA, investigate source
alarm_thresholds.emergency: 30 ppm - Immediate evacuation, respiratory protection required for entry

gases_to_monitor.effects: Eye irritation at 10 ppm, pulmonary edema at 100 ppm, death at 600 ppm within minutes
gases_to_monitor.source_indicators: Water table interaction, ore body chemistry, geothermal activity
gases_to_monitor.special_considerations: Rapid olfactory fatigue means loss of smell does NOT indicate safe levels. Continuous monitoring mandatory.

gases_to_monitor.name: Nitrogen Dioxide
gases_to_monitor.primary_source: Blasting fumes (ANFO and emulsion explosives), diesel exhaust
gases_to_monitor.post_blast_protocol: Minimum 30-minute re-entry wait, then gas testing before personnel entry. If NO2 > 3 ppm, extend wait period and increase ventilation.

gases_to_monitor.name: Sulfur Dioxide
gases_to_monitor.source_indicators: Sulfide ore body oxidation, blasting, diesel equipment

gases_to_monitor.name: Respirable Particulate Matter
gases_to_monitor.calibration_frequency: Quarterly gravimetric validation of real-time instruments

limits.crystalline_silica: 0.025 mg/m³ (MSHA coal), 0.050 mg/m³ (hard rock) as respirable quartz

level_1_warning.action: Stop work, investigate cause, increase ventilation, do not proceed until restored

level_2_critical.action: Evacuate affected area immediately, seal entry, notify mine manager

level_3_emergency.action: Full mine evacuation, activate emergency response plan, do not attempt rescue without SCBA
level_3_emergency.notification: All emergency services, families, regulatory authority

level_1.equipment_restrictions: None, but prepare for potential restrictions

actions: Stop all electrical equipment in affected area
level_2.equipment_restrictions: All non-IS electrical equipment shut down

actions: Withdraw all personnel from affected section
level_3.notification: Mine Manager, Safety Officer, Regulatory Authority

actions: Account for all personnel at surface assembly point
No re-entry without gas testing and authorization
level_4_evacuation.notification: All mine management, Regulatory Authority, Emergency Services

level_1.action: Investigate source, check for fire indicators, increase ventilation
level_1.investigation_scope: Spontaneous combustion indicators, equipment temperature, recent blasting

level_2.action: Evacuate non-essential personnel, investigate aggressively, deploy thermal imaging
level_2.restrictions: No hot work, no diesel equipment in affected area

level_3.action: Immediate evacuation of affected area, deploy emergency ventilation, prepare for firefighting

level_4.threshold: CO at 200 ppm or rapid rise
level_4.action: Full mine evacuation, activate fire emergency response, seal affected area if necessary

level_1.action: Alert personnel, increase ventilation, investigate water sources

level_2.action: Evacuate non-essential personnel, SCBA required for investigation

level_3.action: Immediate evacuation of affected area, SCBA required for any entry, notify emergency services

level_4.action: Full mine evacuation, area quarantine, emergency services standby, no entry without SCBA and safety watch

ground_control.general_requirements: A qualified person must examine ground conditions each shift and after blasting. Ground control plan required per MSHA 30 CFR Part 50/56/57.

rock_mechanics.competent_person: Must hold degree in rock mechanics or geological engineering with minimum 3 years underground experience
rock_mechanics.stress_mapping: In-situ stress measurements required for all openings exceeding 50m depth using overcoring or hydraulic fracturing
rock_mechanics.numerical_modeling: Phase2/RS2 or equivalent finite element modeling required for underground openings >4m span
rock_mechanics.rock_mass_classification: Q-system (Barton), RMR (Bieniawski), and GSI (Hoek) classifications required for all excavations

types: Fully grouted rebar bolts (standard ground conditions)
Friction bolts / Split sets (intermediate support, non-corrosive environments)
Resin encapsulated bolts (sulfide ore bodies, corrosive conditions)
rock_bolts.spacing: Standard 1.5m x 1.5m grid, increased to 1.0m x 1.0m in poor ground
rock_bolts.length: Minimum 1.8m for standard headings, 2.4m for large excavations, minimum 60% of excavation width
rock_bolts.proof_testing: Random sample of 10% bolts proof tested to 150% of design load annually

shotcrete.wet_mix: 380-420 kg cement/m³, 4-6% accelerator, fiber reinforced at 30-40 kg/m³ steel fibers
shotcrete.thickness_minimum: 75mm for permanent support, 100mm for seismic ground, 50mm for temporary
shotcrete.compressive_strength: Minimum 25 MPa at 28 days, 15 MPa at 24 hours
shotcrete.testing: Core sampling every 500m², break testing at 1, 7, and 28 days

steel_sets.application: Heavy ground conditions, high stress zones, fault zones
steel_sets.spacing: 0.6m to 1.5m centers depending on ground conditions
steel_sets.lagging: Timber or steel plate lagging between sets, minimum 25mm steel plate in high stress

seismic_monitoring.system: Full-array microseismic monitoring network with geophones installed in boreholes throughout mine
seismic_monitoring.sensitivity: Capable of detecting events magnitude -1.0 and above
seismic_monitoring.coverage: 100% of active mining areas and 200m buffer zone
seismic_monitoring.response_time: Real-time processing, automated alerts for events >M0.5
seismic_monitoring.protocol: Events >M1.0 trigger ground condition assessment; Events >M2.0 trigger area inspection; Events >M3.0 trigger temporary closure
seismic_monitoring.personnel_threshold: No personnel in active stope faces during seismic events >M1.5

fall_of_ground_prevention.scaling: Mechanical scaling (excavator or scaler) preferred over hand scaling. Hand scaling only with approved scaling bars minimum 1.8m length.
fall_of_ground_prevention.exclusion_zones: Minimum 3m exclusion from unsupported ground at face. No personnel under freshly shotcreted surfaces for minimum 4 hours.
fall_of_ground_prevention.barrier_systems: De-rating barriers at 20m intervals in stope access drives, catch fences at stope access points
fall_of_ground_prevention.visual_inspection: Every travelway, working face, and development heading must be visually inspected before each work shift

survey_monitoring.convergence_monitoring: Convergence stations installed in all major excavations, read weekly during active mining, monthly during standby
survey_monitoring.prism_monitoring: Automated total station monitoring of critical shafts and surface infrastructure above mining, reading frequency daily
survey_monitoring.inclinometer_monitoring: Monthly readings of surface slope instability areas above underground workings
survey_monitoring.data_management: All monitoring data uploaded to cloud dashboard within 24 hours, automated alerts for threshold exceedances

refuge_chambers.regulatory_basis: MSHA 30 CFR Part 75 Subpart K (coal) and Part 75.1700-1704

requirements.coal_mines: Permanently installed refuge alternatives within 1,500 feet travel distance for all underground personnel. Temporary refuge alternatives may be used during development.
requirements.metal_nonmetal: MSHA requires evacuation plan, refuge alternatives considered for each mine. Many operations install voluntarily.
requirements.travel_distance: Maximum 1,500 feet (457m) to nearest refuge chamber from any work location in coal mines
requirements.capacity: Minimum 150 cubic feet per person accommodated (approximately 4.25 m³ per person)
requirements.survival_time: Minimum 48 hours at maximum occupancy, 96 hours for new installations
requirements.air_supply: Self-contained air supply at 0.5 m³/s per person, minimum 48-hour capacity. CO scrubbing to maintain below 100 ppm.

type_a_permanent.construction: Reinforced concrete or steel modular construction, rated for ground fall resistance
type_a_permanent.sealing: Positive pressure sealing system, smoke-tight doors
type_a_permanent.air_system: Compressed air manifold connection from mine supply + independent backup cylinders
type_a_permanent.carbon_dioxide_scrubber: Lithium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide chemical scrubber, 48-hour capacity
type_a_permanent.carbon_monoxide_scrubber: Hopcalite catalyst bed, converts CO to CO2, capacity for 48 hours at 200 ppm input
type_a_permanent.communication: Hardwired telephone to surface, two-way radio, surface monitoring beacon
type_a_permanent.water: Minimum 1 liter per person per hour for 48 hours, supplied from mine potable water system
type_a_permanent.sanitation: Chemical toilet, waste bags, basic sanitation supplies
type_a_permanent.first_aid: Complete first aid kit, trauma supplies, AED
type_a_permanent.signage: Illuminated signs every 200m directing to nearest chamber, reflective path markers on floor

type_b_portable.use_case: Temporary operations, development headings, remote locations
type_b_portable.air_supply: Self-contained compressed air cylinders, 36-hour minimum duration
type_b_portable.food_water: Emergency food rations (high calorie bars), 1L water per person per 8 hours
type_b_portable.communication: Two-way radio, emergency beacon, messenger system backup

inspection_schedule.daily: Visual inspection of door, seals, signage, and access clear of obstructions
inspection_schedule.weekly: Functional test of communication systems, air supply pressure check
inspection_schedule.monthly: Full inspection including air quality sampling, first aid kit inventory, food/water rotation
inspection_schedule.quarterly: Comprehensive inspection by qualified person including structural assessment
inspection_schedule.annually: Full system test with timed drill from furthest work point

post_incident_procedure.activation: Personnel enter chamber, seal doors, activate monitoring and communication
post_incident_procedure.communication: Establish contact with surface rescue team, provide headcount and conditions
post_incident_procedure.air_management: Monitor CO2 and O2 levels, manage air supply, report any smoke or gas ingress
post_incident_procedure.discipline: Remain in chamber until rescue team arrives and provides all-clear, no unauthorized exit

emergency_evacuation.evacuation_plan_requirements: Written plan approved by mine manager, reviewed quarterly, updated after any significant change. Per MSHA 30 CFR 75.1700.

primary_escape_routes.number_of_exits: Minimum 2 separate escape routes from every underground location, routes must not converge until reaching surface
primary_escape_routes.route_marking: Illuminated directional signs every 50m, reflective markers at eye level, floor-level luminous strips
primary_escape_routes.route_width: Minimum 1.2m clear width maintained at all times
primary_escape_routes.self_rescuer_deployment: Self-rescuer stations at 250m intervals along all escape routes, additional units at every intersection
primary_escape_routes.travel_time: Maximum 30-minute travel time to surface or refuge chamber from any location

self_rescuers.type: Chemical oxygen self-rescuer (e.g., DRÄGER OXY 6000, MSA IR Pass), 60-minute rated duration
self_rescuers.carrying_requirement: Every underground worker must carry a self-rescuer at all times when underground
self_rescuers.deployment_time: Must be deployable within 30 seconds, workers drilled to don in <15 seconds
self_rescuers.training: Quarterly donning drills under simulated smoke conditions, annual refresher with written assessment
self_rescuers.inspection: Monthly weight check (indicates seal integrity), monthly visual inspection, replace per manufacturer schedule
self_rescuers.locations: Wall-mounted stations at intersections, near refuge chambers, at working face entry points

evacuation_signals.primary: Continuous siren + flashing lights for 3 minutes = immediate evacuation
evacuation_signals.secondary: Three short blasts on air horn = immediate evacuation
evacuation_signals.all_clear: One long blast followed by verbal confirmation = all clear, safe to return
evacuation_signals.communication: All personnel must acknowledge all-clear signal before returning underground

accountability.check_in_system: Electronic tag-in/tag-out system at all portal entries, cage stations, and refuge chambers
accountability.headcount_verification: Surface control room maintains real-time headcount of all underground personnel
accountability.post_evacuation: Assembly point headcount within 15 minutes of surface arrival, report missing persons immediately
accountability.missing_personnel: Activate search and rescue within 5 minutes if personnel unaccounted for after evacuation

primary_systems.coverage: Continuous coverage along all active underground workings via radiating coaxial cable
primary_systems.frequency: VHF band, typically 30-50 MHz analog or digital
primary_systems.redundancy: Dual cable feeds from different surface locations

primary_systems.coverage: All active development headings and decline access routes
primary_systems.standard: 802.11ax or 802.11ac, industrial-grade access points rated IP67

primary_systems.locations: Refuge chambers, pump stations, shaft stations, underground workshops
primary_systems.type_specification: Explosion-proof or intrinsically safe per installation environment

primary_systems.technology: Through-the-earth signaling using ultra-low frequency electromagnetic signals
primary_systems.capability: One-way text messaging from surface to underground, functional even during ground failure
primary_systems.usage: Emergency signaling to trapped miners, activation of refuge chamber communication

personnel_tracking.technology: RFID tags worn by all underground workers, readers at all access points and intersections
personnel_tracking.accuracy: Zone-level location (within 100m) in standard areas, near-exact location near readers
personnel_tracking.data_retention: Minimum 1 year of tracking data stored for investigation purposes
personnel_tracking.privacy: Data used only for safety purposes, not for performance monitoring

testing_schedule.daily: Radio communication test all sections before shift start
testing_schedule.weekly: PED transmission test, leaky feeder signal strength survey
testing_schedule.monthly: Full communication system integrity test including backup systems

hierarchy_of_controls: Elimination - Remove person from hazard zone through automation
Engineering controls - Camera systems, proximity detection, physical barriers
Administrative controls - Traffic management plans, training, procedures

proximity_detection.technology: Wi-Fi or UWB based proximity awareness systems (e.g., Hexagon, Modular Mining)
proximity_detection.exclusion_zone: No personnel within 50m of operating haul truck unless both truck and personnel are stationary with engine off

dumping_protocols.berm_height: Minimum 75% of largest tire diameter, minimum 1.2m height
dumping_protocols.berm_material: Consolidated competent material, inspected before each shift, repaired immediately if damaged
dumping_protocols.approach_speed: Maximum 10 km/h approaching dump edge, maximum 5 km/h for final positioning
dumping_protocols.dumping_position: Truck to be perpendicular to dump face, full steering lock left or right for quick escape
dumping_protocols.edge_distance: Minimum 3m from dump edge to rear axle when dumping
dumping_protocols.spotter_requirement: Spotter required for reverse maneuvers within 30m of dump edge
dumping_protocols.load_limits: Maximum payload ±5% as marked on truck. Weighbridge check for new operators.

maintenance_safety.lockout_tagout: All energy sources isolated and locked before any maintenance. Hydraulic pressure relieved, battery disconnected, air systems bled.
maintenance_safety.working_heights: Fall protection required above 1.8m. Guardrails on all elevated maintenance platforms.
maintenance_safety.lift_points: Only manufacturer-designated lift points used. Rated slings and hardware. Qualified rigger required.
maintenance_safety.tire_service: Inflation cages required for tires exceeding 1.2m diameter. Pressure rated for 110% of working pressure.
maintenance_safety.hydraulic_systems: Hydraulic pressure tested to 150% operating pressure annually. All hoses replaced per manufacturer schedule regardless of condition.

fatigue_management.shift_limits: Maximum 12-hour shifts, maximum 60 hours per week
fatigue_management.fatigue_monitoring: Wearable fatigue detection devices (e.g., Caterpillar DSS, Seeing Machines Guardian)
fatigue_management.intervention_threshold: Microsleep detected = immediate removal from operation, mandatory 30-minute rest minimum
fatigue_management.roster_design: Minimum 11 hours between shifts. Night shift rotation maximum 5 consecutive nights.
fatigue_management.environmental_controls: Cab temperature maintained at 20-24°C, ergonomic seat with lumbar support, anti-glare displays

hazard_zones.primary_crusher_feed: Exclusion zone during operation. No personnel within 15m of hopper during dumping.
hazard_zones.crusher_chamber: Lockout/tagout required for any access. Zero energy verification before entry.
hazard_zones.conveyor_transfer_points: Nip points marked with guards. No reaching across or under running conveyors.
hazard_zones.secondary_crushing: Noise levels typically >115 dB - hearing protection mandatory at all times.

lockout_procedures.step_1: Notify control room of maintenance intent
lockout_procedures.step_2: Shut down crusher using local isolator
lockout_procedures.step_3: Lock and tag isolator with personal padlock
lockout_procedures.step_4: Verify zero energy - attempt restart from local and remote controls
lockout_procedures.step_5: Bleed hydraulic pressure, block flywheels/jaws if applicable
lockout_procedures.step_6: Install additional mechanical blocks on rotating components
lockout_procedures.step_7: Test for residual energy before commencing work
lockout_procedures.step_8: Maintain lockout throughout maintenance, only authorized person removes lock

dust_control.water_sprays: High-pressure spray bars at all transfer points, minimum 200 kPa water pressure
dust_control.dust_extraction: Baghouse or cyclone extraction at crusher discharge, minimum 95% collection efficiency
dust_control.monitoring: Continuous PM10 and PM2.5 monitoring at crusher perimeter and community boundary
dust_control.suppression_agents: Anionic surfactant dosing at 1:500 ratio for sticky ore types

controls: Enclosed operator cabin with sound insulation to <85 dB(A)
Acoustic enclosures around vibrating screens and crushers
Engineered sound barriers around crusher building perimeter
Personal hearing protection mandatory when >85 dB(A) for 8+ hours
noise_management.audiometric_testing: Baseline audiogram within first 6 months, annual monitoring audiogram thereafter

access_restrictions.running_conveyors: No riding on conveyors. No walking on conveyors. No working on or near running conveyors without specific safe work procedure.
access_restrictions.emergency_pull_cords: Emergency stop pull cords on both sides of conveyor, maximum 30m intervals, tested each shift
access_restrictions.belt_tracking: Belt tracking and tensioning only performed on stopped, isolated conveyor

guarding.nip_points: All nip points guarded to prevent contact. Guards extend minimum 2m from nip point.
guarding.return_idlers: Guards on all return side idlers within 2m of walkway
guarding.drives: Belt drives fully enclosed in locked guard, V-belt drives in mesh guard
guarding.take_ups: Hydraulic take-up units guarded. Spring take-ups in enclosed housing.
guarding.walkways: Minimum 600mm wide walkway on one side of all conveyors >15m length, handrails on both sides if elevated >1m

fire_protection.detection: Linear heat detection cable along entire belt length, infrared scanning at drive and tail pulleys
fire_protection.suppression: Water spray system activated by fire detection or manual pull station
fire_protection.extinguishers: ABC dry chemical extinguishers at 100m intervals along conveyor
fire_protection.belt_material: Fire-resistant belts per AS 1333 / DIN 22109, self-extinguishing within 30 seconds of flame removal
fire_protection.spillage: Belt cleaners and scrapers to prevent material buildup that can cause friction fire

personnel_crossing.designated_crossings: Personnel crossings at maximum 200m intervals, clearly signposted
personnel_crossing.crossing_construction: Walk-under or walk-over with handrails and slip-resistant surfaces
personnel_crossing.prohibition: No crossing under or over running conveyor except at designated crossings

respirable_crystalline_silica.source: Drilling, blasting, crushing, screening of siliceous material
respirable_crystalline_silica.health_effects: Silicosis, lung cancer, COPD, kidney disease

coal_dust.source: Coal mining, coal handling, coal processing

welding_fume.permissible_exposure: Varies by metal - iron oxide 10 mg/m³, manganese 5 mg/m³ (TWA)

suppression_systems.application: Crusher feed points, conveyor transfers, haul roads, stockpile faces
suppression_systems.water_consumption: 0.5-2.0 L/min per nozzle depending on application

suppression_systems.application: Haul roads (water carts), stockpile areas, general area dust control

suppression_systems.application_rate: 0.5-2.0 L/m² depending on product and traffic
suppression_systems.effectiveness: 60-90% reduction in fine particle generation, lasts 2-6 weeks

suppression_systems.application: Drill holes during drilling, continuous miner cutting head, crusher feed

air_quality_monitoring.fixed_monitors: PM10 and PM2.5 monitors at pit perimeter, community boundaries, and processing plant
air_quality_monitoring.personal_monitors: Personal dataRAM or gravimetric samplers for workers in high-dust areas
air_quality_monitoring.reporting: Daily monitoring, weekly trend analysis, monthly reporting to management

triggers.action: PM10 > 100 μg/m³ 24-hour average at community boundary
triggers.shutdown: PM10 > 250 μg/m³ 1-hour average at any monitoring station

regulatory_limits.iso_standard: ISO 1999:2013 - Acoustics - Determination of occupational noise exposure

measurement_methods.area_monitoring: Sound level meter with octave band analysis, IEC 61672 Class 1
measurement_methods.personal_monitoring: Dosimetry with personal noise dosimeters, minimum 4-hour measurement period
measurement_methods.frequency: Area monitoring at commissioning, annually, and after equipment changes. Personal monitoring for all workers in >85 dBA areas.

hearing_conservation_program.audiometric_testing: Baseline within 6 months of hire, annual monitoring audiogram
hearing_conservation_program.standard_threshold_shift: STS of ≥10 dB average at 2000, 3000, 4000 Hz triggers review

hearing_protection.85_to_100_dba: Hearing protection mandatory, single protection (plug or muff)
hearing_protection.above_100_dba: Double hearing protection mandatory (plug AND muff)
hearing_protection.above_115_dba: Maximum 15-minute exposure without engineering controls, double protection mandatory

engineering_controls: Vibration isolation mounts for rotating equipment
Barriers and berms between noise sources and work areas

cyanide_management.icmc_code: International Cyanide Management Code (ICMC) for the Manufacture, Transport, and Use of Cyanide in the Production of Gold (2017 revision)

calcium_cyanide.usage: Heap leach operations, some flotation circuits

facility_design.construction: Reinforced concrete with chemical-resistant coating (epoxy or vinyl ester)
facility_design.ventilation: Forced ventilation with minimum 6 air changes per hour, gas detection at ceiling level
facility_design.secondary_containment: 110% capacity containment bund, chemical-resistant liner, leak detection system
facility_design.segregation: Minimum 30m from waterways, drainage systems, and stormwater. 100m from populated areas. Separate from acids and oxidizers.
facility_design.security: Perimeter fence with razor wire, CCTV, restricted access, 24/7 security presence
facility_design.signage: Poison gas warnings, emergency contact numbers, spill response procedures in local language

inventory_management.tracking: Real-time inventory monitoring with automated level sensors
inventory_management.reporting: Daily reconciliation of receipts, usage, and stock levels
inventory_management.records: Minimum 5-year record retention for all cyanide transactions
inventory_management.audit: Annual third-party audit per ICMC requirements

transportation.vehicle_requirements: Dedicated cyanide transport vehicles, double-walled tanks, GPS tracking
transportation.driver_training: Cyanide-specific transport training, HAZMAT certification, defensive driving
transportation.documentation: Dangerous goods manifest, emergency response information, SDS accompanying all shipments
transportation.route_planning: Avoid populated areas where possible, pre-planned emergency stop locations
transportation.spill_kits: Minimum 2 spill kits per vehicle containing neutralization agents (sodium hypochlorite, ferrous sulfate)

immediate_actions: Sound alarm, evacuate upwind and uphill
Notify emergency response team and site manager
Do NOT enter spill zone without full PPE including SCBA

containment.diking: Use earth, sand, or absorbent booms to prevent entry into waterways
containment.covering: Cover spill with plastic sheeting to prevent rain wash into drains
containment.pumping: Use explosion-proof, intrinsically safe pumps for liquid recovery

neutralization.sodium_hypochlorite: 5-15% solution applied to spill area. Contact time minimum 30 minutes. pH maintained >10.5.
neutralization.ferrous_sulfate: Application to cyanide solutions converts cyanide to less toxic ferrocyanide complexes
neutralization.hydrogen_peroxide: 35% H2O2 added to cyanide solutions under alkaline conditions, converts cyanide to cyanate
neutralization.verification: Post-neutralization sampling to confirm cyanide concentration below 10 mg/L before disposal

water_contamination.threshold: Total cyanide > 1.0 mg/L in surface water triggers emergency response
water_contamination.notification: Environmental regulatory authority notified within 2 hours of discovery
water_contamination.remediation: Pump and treat, activated carbon adsorption, or chemical oxidation depending on concentration

immediate_treatment.step_1: Move victim to fresh air immediately
immediate_treatment.step_2: Call emergency services, state cyanide poisoning
immediate_treatment.step_3: Administer antidote kit if available and trained
immediate_treatment.step_4: Begin CPR if breathing has stopped
immediate_treatment.step_5: Remove contaminated clothing, flush skin/eyes with water for 15+ minutes

contents: Amyl nitrite inhalers (x6) - immediate while preparing IV
antidote_kit.hydroxocobalamin_administration: 5g IV over 15 minutes, may repeat once
antidote_kit.sodium_nitrite_administration: 300mg (10mL of 3%) IV over 3-5 minutes, monitor for methemoglobinemia
antidote_kit.storage: Minimum 2 kits per 25 personnel in cyanide area, stored in climate-controlled cabinet, checked monthly

elemental_mercury.vapor_pressure: 1.27 × 10⁻³ kPa at 20°C - significant vapor at room temperature
elemental_mercury.health_effects: Tremors, cognitive impairment, kidney damage, neurological damage, Minamata disease

methylmercury.bioaccumulation: Bioaccumulates in aquatic food chain, magnification factor >1000x
methylmercury.primary_exposure: Consumption of contaminated fish, occupational in gold processing

minimum_ppe: Air-purifying respirator with mercury vapor cartridge (OV/AG)
Nitrile gloves minimum 8 mil thickness, double gloving
Chemical splash goggles or full-face shield
personal_protection.supplied_air: Required when Hg vapor exceeds 5× PEL (0.25 mg/m³) or in confined spaces
personal_protection.decontamination: Mercury-specific decontamination station with cold water wash and sulfur powder for residual detection

procedure: Evacuate immediate area
Ventilate area, close doors
Wear mercury PPE
Use mercury squeegee and aspirator (never use vacuum cleaner)
Place mercury in airtight container with water cover
Apply sulfur powder to area where droplets may have spread

large_spill.definition: Greater than 5mL or spill in enclosed space
procedure: Evacuate entire area, establish exclusion zone
Emergency ventilation, DO NOT turn off HVAC (spreads vapor)
Trained hazmat response team only
Mercury vapor monitoring until below 0.025 mg/m³
Professional mercury remediation for porous surfaces

prohibited_actions: DO NOT use household vacuum cleaner (vaporizes mercury)
DO NOT use compressed air to clean mercury
DO NOT pour mercury down drains
DO NOT wash mercury-contaminated clothing with other laundry

waste_disposal.elemental_mercury: Licensed hazardous waste facility, triple-contained packaging, DOT shipping
waste_disposal.contaminated_materials: Sealed containers, labeled, transported per hazardous waste regulations
waste_disposal.monitoring_waste: Amalgam, test kits, sampling equipment - collected and stored for licensed disposal
waste_disposal.record_keeping: Full cradle-to-grave manifesting, annual reporting to regulatory authority

regulatory_framework: IME (Institute of Makers of Explosives) Recommendations

emulsion_explosives.detonation_velocity: 4,500-6,000 m/s depending on confinement and density

anfo.limitations: Not water resistant, sensitivity degrades in wet conditions
anfo.detonation_velocity: 2,300-4,500 m/s depending on confinement and diameter

detonators.electric_detonators: Instantaneous or millisecond delay, R-1 type for underground
detonators.non_electric_detonators: Nonel tubes with millisecond delays, shock tube initiation
detonators.electronic_detonators: Programmable delays (±0.1ms accuracy), anti-misfire, test capability
detonators.blasting_cables: Trunklines, surface bus wires, downhole cables - all per MSHA standards

primers.cast_boosters: Pentolite or PETN-based, minimum 200g PETN equivalent for each column charge
primers.detonating_cord: 30-65 grains/ft PETN core, used for surface initiation and downhole connections

surface_magazines.distance_from_habitation: Minimum distances per ATF Table 273.9 based on net explosive weight
surface_magazines.construction: Type 4 magazine (reinforced concrete, steel-lined) or Type 2 (wood frame, metal-lined)
surface_magazines.ventilation: Natural ventilation through screened louvers at floor and ceiling level
surface_magazines.lightning_protection: Complete lightning protection system per NFPA 780
surface_magazines.grounding: All metal components bonded and grounded, ground resistance <10 ohms
surface_magazines.fire_protection: ABC fire extinguishers, 3m clearance from vegetation, no open flames within 30m
surface_magazines.access: Double padlock, two-person access control, visitor log

underground_magazines.location: Away from travelways, electrical installations, and oil/grease storage
underground_magazines.separation: Minimum 50m from active workings, separated by solid rock pillar
underground_magazines.construction: Rock-cut chamber with smooth blasting, no steel supports that could become projectiles
underground_magazines.storage_limits: Maximum 48-hour supply of explosives per underground magazine

transport_to_face.vehicle_requirements: Approved explosives transport vehicle, flameproof, spark arrestor
transport_to_face.quantity_limits: Maximum 200kg per transport trip underground, no detonators with explosives in same vehicle
transport_to_face.routing: Pre-determined routes, no passing through active blasting zones
transport_to_face.personnel: Trained blaster only, escort if required by regulation

pre_blast: Confirm blast pattern and charge plan approved by shotfirer
All personnel accounted for and withdrawn to safe distance
Warning signals sounded (minimum 3 warnings before firing)
Electrical equipment within blast zone shut down and isolated if required
Gas testing in confined areas completed

firing_sequence.misfire_management: Minimum 15-minute wait after last detonation before investigation. No re-entry for 30 minutes. Misfire procedures per site-specific plan.
firing_sequence.surface_firing: From designated firing point, clear line of sight or CCTV monitoring
firing_sequence.underground_firing: From protected station with communication to all access points
firing_sequence.initiation_systems: Electronic detonators preferred for controlled fragmentation and reduced vibration

post_blast: Minimum 30-minute ventilation period (hard rock), longer for coal
Atmospheric testing before re-entry: CO <25ppm, NO2 <3ppm, CH4 <1% (coal)
Visual examination of face and back by competent person
Misfire investigation if any suspect detonations

blast_vibration_limits.residential_structures: 12.5 mm/s peak particle velocity (PPV) at nearest residence
blast_vibration_limits.mine_infrastructure: 100 mm/s PPV for concrete structures, 50 mm/s for shotcreted ground
blast_vibration_limits.monitoring: Seismograph at nearest sensitive structure for every blast, daily review of data

competent_person_requirements.qualifications: Certified shotfirer/blaster per state/provincial requirements, minimum 2 years supervised blasting experience
responsibilities: Design and supervise all blasting operations

types_managed.reactivity: Exothermic reaction with water - always add acid to water, never reverse

types_managed.exposure_limits: ACGIH TLV: 2 ppm (ceiling), OSHA PEL: 5 ppm (ceiling)

types_managed.special_hazard: Strong oxidizer - contact with organic materials may cause fire
Generates significant heat when dissolved - exothermic

secondary_containment.capacity: 110% of largest tank volume OR 25% of total storage volume, whichever is greater
secondary_containment.material: Chemical-resistant: HDPE liner (min 2mm), acid-resistant brick with epoxy coating, or FRP
secondary_containment.sump: Collection sump with detection, automatic pump to waste treatment
secondary_containment.testing: Annual integrity testing, visual inspection quarterly

ventilation.acid_areas: Forced ventilation with minimum 6 air changes per hour
ventilation.gas_detection: Continuous monitoring for acid vapors (HCl, SO2, NO2), alarm at 50% of STEL
ventilation.scrubbing: Caustic scrubber on vent stack if near sensitive receptor

minimum_ppe: Chemical-resistant gloves (neoprene, minimum 15 mil, or butyl rubber)
Chemical-resistant boots (steel toe, PVC or rubber)
Respiratory: Half-face APR with acid gas/organic vapor cartridges, or supplied air in confined space
personal_protection.eyewash: ANSI Z358.1 eyewash station within 10 seconds walking distance of acid handling
personal_protection.shower: Emergency shower within 10 seconds walking distance of acid handling

incompatible: Carbon steel (sulfuric acid at high temp)

procedure: Don acid-resistant PPE
Contain with inert absorbent (vermiculite, dry sand)
DO NOT use sawdust or combustible absorbents with oxidizing acids
Neutralize with sodium bicarbonate or lime slurry
Collect and dispose as hazardous waste
Evacuate area, establish exclusion zone
Notify emergency response team
Contain with dikes to prevent entry to drains or waterways
Neutralize from perimeter inward
Flush area with large volumes of water after neutralization
Collect all contaminated water for treatment

acid_to_water_mixing.rule: ALWAYS add acid to water - NEVER add water to acid
acid_to_water_mixing.reason: Exothermic reaction can cause violent boiling and spattering
acid_to_water_mixing.exception: If water contacts acid inadvertently, evacuate immediately and allow to cool before approach

minimum_mandatory.standard: ANSI Z89.1 Type I Class E (electrical rated)
minimum_mandatory.replacement_trigger: Any impact, 5 years from manufacture date, or visible damage
minimum_mandatory.accessories: Integrated chin strap for working at heights or in windy conditions

minimum_mandatory.lens_type: Anti-scratch, anti-fog coating, clear or tinted as conditions require
minimum_mandatory.prescription: Prescription safety glasses available, prescription inserts for safety goggles

minimum_mandatory.visibility: Retroreflective strips visible from all angles, fluorescent background material
minimum_mandatory.underground_specification: Class 2 for travelways, Class 3 for surface work near vehicles

minimum_mandatory.features: Steel toe (200J impact), steel midsole (puncture resistant), slip-resistant sole, electrical hazard rated

types.earplugs: Foam (NRR 29-33 dB) or pre-molded reusable (NRR 25-27 dB)
types.earmuffs: NRR 25-31 dB, over hard hat compatible models available
types.double_protection: Plug AND muff required when >100 dB(A)

minimum_mandatory.carrying: Attached to belt or in pouch at waist, within easy reach at all times underground
minimum_mandatory.training: Quarterly donning drill, must deploy in <30 seconds

minimum_mandatory.standard: NIOSH-approved filtering facepiece (N95 minimum) or half-face APR for dusty conditions
minimum_mandatory.fit_testing: Annual quantitative fit test for all respirator users

welding.helmet: Auto-darkening welding helmet, DIN 9-13 shade, with side shields
welding.gloves: Leather welding gloves, gauntlet cuff, minimum 300mm length
welding.respiratory: Powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) with welding filter for confined work

heights_work.harness: Full-body harness per ANSI Z359.11 or AS/NZS 1891.1
heights_work.lanyard: Shock-absorbing lanyard, maximum 2m deployed, double-leg for 100% tie-off
heights_work.anchor_point: Certified anchor point rated to 15kN minimum, above head height
heights_work.rescue_plan: Pre-planned rescue procedure for fall arrest, retrieval within 15 minutes

shotcrete.respiratory: Full-face PAPR or supplied air respirator
shotcrete.body_protection: Waterproof coveralls under hard hat, chemical-resistant boots
shotcrete.skin_protection: Barrier cream on exposed skin, full coverage clothing

vehicle_operations.high_visibility_clothing: Class 3 vest or jacket when working within 50m of mobile equipment
vehicle_operations.hard_hat: ANSI Z89.1 Type I Class E with integrated sun peak
vehicle_operations.safety_footwear: Steel toe cap, cut-resistant, heat-resistant sole, ankle support
vehicle_operations.hearing_protection: Required within 30m of operating heavy equipment
vehicle_operations.seat_belt: Mandatory in all mobile equipment, integrated reminders

drilling_operations.hearing_protection: Minimum double protection (plug + muff) due to >110 dB(A) exposure
drilling_operations.respiratory: P100 particulate filter for dry drilling, minimum; supplied air for known gas zones
drilling_operations.vibration_gloves: Anti-vibration gloves per ISO 10819 for prolonged drill operation
drilling_operations.face_shield: Clear face shield for drill stem handling, mesh shield for blast hole collar operations

crushing_screening.respiratory: Half-face APR with P100 filter minimum, PAPR for dusty operations
crushing_screening.hearing_protection: Mandatory double protection within 15m of crusher
crushing_screening.body_protection: High-visibility long-sleeve shirt, long pants, steel-toe boots
crushing_screening.cut_resistance: Cut-resistant gloves (Level A4 minimum) for screen deck work

flotation_area.chemical_exposure_risk: Frothers (MIBC, pine oil), collectors (xanthates, dithiophosphates), depressants (cyanide, lime), pH modifiers
flotation_area.respiratory: Half-face APR with OV/AG cartridges when chemical concentrations exceed OEL
flotation_area.gloves: Nitrile or neoprene chemical-resistant gloves, minimum 8 mil thickness
flotation_area.eyewash: Must be within 10 seconds walk from any chemical handling point
flotation_area.splash_protection: Chemical splash apron and face shield during reagent mixing

thermal_protection.radiant_heat_shield: Aluminized proximity suit for work within 3m of hot surfaces (>200°C)
thermal_protection.face_shield: Gold-tinted face shield for radiant heat protection
thermal_protection.boots: Heat-resistant boots rated to 300°C contact temperature

kiln_area.respiratory: Full-face supplied air for confined space entry into kiln
kiln_area.monitoring: Continuous heat stress monitoring with core temperature telemetry

laboratory.acid_handling: Fume hood for all acid digestion, splash goggles, nitrile gloves, lab coat
laboratory.fire_safety: Class B fire extinguisher within 5m, fire blanket, eyewash within 3m
laboratory.chemical_storage: Locked cabinet for acids, oxidizers stored separately from flammables
laboratory.waste_disposal: Segregated waste containers, labeled, collected by licensed waste contractor

general_principles: Always read SDS before handling any chemical
Minimize exposure through engineering controls first
Use least hazardous chemical substitute where feasible
Maintain air monitoring in chemical handling areas
Emergency shower and eyewash within 10 seconds walk of all chemical use areas

xanthate.respiratory: Half-face APR with OV cartridge for mixing operations
xanthate.body: Long sleeve shirt, long pants, chemical-resistant apron for mixing

sodium_cyanide.gloves: Double nitrile gloves, minimum 12 mil combined
sodium_cyanide.respiratory: Full-face APR with OV/AG cartridges, or supplied air
sodium_cyanide.eye_protection: Full-face shield integral with respiratory protection

sulfuric_acid.gloves: Butyl rubber minimum 15 mil, or neoprene
sulfuric_acid.respiratory: Half-face APR with acid gas cartridge
sulfuric_acid.body: Acid-resistant apron, rubber boots, long sleeves

frothers_mibc.respiratory: Organic vapor cartridge when above OEL
frothers_mibc.body: Standard work clothing with long sleeves

storage_compatibility.acids: Separate from bases, oxidizers, and flammables. Secondary containment required.
storage_compatibility.bases: Separate from acids. Secondary containment required.
storage_compatibility.oxidizers: Separate from flammables, organics, and reducing agents.
storage_compatibility.flammables: Approved flammable storage cabinet, separate from oxidizers and acids.
storage_compatibility.cyanides: Separate from acids (generates HCN gas). Dedicated locked storage.

fire_categories_in_mining.class_a: Ordinary combustibles - timber, rubber, cloth (underground support materials, conveyor belts)
fire_categories_in_mining.class_b: Flammable liquids - diesel fuel, hydraulic oil, lubricants
fire_categories_in_mining.class_d: Metal fires - lithium batteries, aluminum dust (rare but possible)

immediate_actions: Activate fire alarm (pull station or radio call)
Close fire doors and ventilation stoppings to isolate affected zone
Attempt to fight fire ONLY if: small, trained, PPE available, clear escape route maintained
Report fire location, size, and type to control room

firefighting_equipment.portable_extinguishers: ABC dry chemical at all intersections, CO2 at electrical installations, foam at fuel storage
firefighting_equipment.fire_hose_reels: 150mm hose reels at 100m intervals in development headings
firefighting_equipment.self-contained_extinguishers: Water grenades, fire suppression balls at refuge chamber locations
firefighting_equipment.fire_suppression_systems: Fixed water spray on conveyor drives, deluge systems in transformer chambers
firefighting_equipment.diesel_fire_suppression: Automatic fire suppression systems on all diesel equipment (AFFF or dry chemical)

fire_stop_systems.passive_fire_doors: Fire-resistant doors in all airways, self-closing, rated minimum 4 hours
fire_stop_systems.active_fire_stoppings: Concrete block stoppings with fire doors, ventilated to prevent pressure buildup
fire_stop_systems.ventilation_control: Ability to reverse main fan, close/redirect ventilation to starve fire of oxygen
fire_stop_systems.sealing: Permanent seals with foam injection capability for uncontrolled fires

surface_fire_response.sprinkler_systems: NFPA 13 sprinkler systems in processing plant, warehouse, and workshop buildings
surface_fire_response.fire_water_system: Dedicated fire water ring main with hydrants at 150m intervals, minimum 10 bar pressure
surface_fire_response.fire_pump: Electric fire pump with diesel backup, automatic start on pressure drop
surface_fire_response.foam_systems: AFFF foam systems for fuel storage areas, proportioning system tested monthly

fire_investigation.scene_preservation: Secure fire scene, photograph extensively before disturbance
fire_investigation.cause_determination: Investigate all fires >$10,000 damage or any injury fire. Root cause analysis.
fire_investigation.reporting: Regulatory authority notification within 24 hours for significant fires
fire_investigation.corrective_actions: Implement findings within 30 days, verify effectiveness within 90 days

flood_risk_assessment.assessment_frequency: Annual comprehensive review, triggered review after significant rain event or geological change

monitoring_systems.underground_water: Piezometers in all boreholes, flow meters in mine sumps, level indicators in water bodies above workings
monitoring_systems.weather_monitoring: On-site automatic weather station, integration with national meteorological service, flash flood warnings
monitoring_systems.dam_monitoring: Piezometers in dam walls, seepage flow measurement, survey monitoring of wall movement

alarm_thresholds.yellow_alert: Water level rising at >0.5m/hour in any monitored point
alarm_thresholds.orange_alert: Water inflow exceeding pumping capacity by >50%
alarm_thresholds.red_alert: Dam wall movement exceeding 5mm/day, or uncontrolled water ingress

pumping_capacity.design_capacity: Pumping system rated for maximum anticipated inflow + 50% safety margin
pumping_capacity.redundancy: Minimum two independent pump systems, each capable of handling 75% of design flow
pumping_capacity.power: Dual power feed for pumping systems, diesel backup pump capability
pumping_capacity.maintenance: Monthly pump test at full capacity, impeller inspection quarterly

evacuation_procedure.trigger: Any warning of imminent flooding, water rising faster than pumps can manage
evacuation_procedure.communication: Siren alarm + radio announcement + telephone notification to all underground personnel
evacuation_procedure.routes: Designated flood evacuation routes avoiding low points, directed to highest accessible point
evacuation_procedure.personnel_tracking: Real-time headcount to confirm all personnel evacuated above flood level
evacuation_procedure.rescue_operations: Boat rescue teams on standby during high-risk periods, dive teams available for post-flood assessment

types.prevention: Competent person examination, proper support design, exclusion zones, seismic monitoring
types.response: Evacuate affected area, seal entry, investigate from safe position, deploy rescue if personnel trapped

types.prevention: Stope design based on rock mechanics assessment, pillar design factors, backfill where required
types.response: Full area evacuation, seismic assessment, surface monitoring for subsidence, search and rescue

types.prevention: Shaft monitoring, ground improvement around shaft, proper shaft lining design
types.response: Evacuate shaft, assess stability from surface, rescue via secondary egress if available

types.prevention: Subsidence modeling, surface infrastructure setback from mining, monitoring prisms on surface structures
types.response: Evacuate affected surface area, restrict access, emergency stabilization if required

types.prevention: Geotechnical slope design, drainage systems, monitoring inclinometers and prisms, catch benches
types.response: Evacuate failure zone, restrict access, geotechnical assessment before re-entry

rescue_operations.stabilization: Re-support failed area from safe position before rescue team entry, temporary ventilation
rescue_operations.time_criticality: First 24 hours critical for survival, establish communication with trapped persons ASAP

methane_inundation.source: Sudden liberation from coal seams or gas-bearing formations
methane_inundation.mechanism: Intersection of gas-bearing fracture, failure of gas drainage system, borehole breakout
methane_inundation.immediate_danger: Explosion risk, asphyxiation at high concentrations

co2_inundation.source: CO2-bearing formations, combustion products, oxidation of coal
co2_inundation.mechanism: Sudden liberation from confined formations, overturning of CO2-rich water
co2_inundation.concentration_potential: CO2 at >5% causes unconsciousness, >10% fatal within minutes
co2_inundation.warning_signs: CO2 monitors in return air, unusual water bubbling, dead vegetation in boreholes

h2s_inundation.source: Water-bearing formations with sulfate-reducing bacteria, volcanic geology
h2s_inundation.concentration_potential: Can reach hundreds of ppm rapidly
h2s_inundation.immediate_danger: IDLH at 100 ppm, unconsciousness within breaths at 500+ ppm
h2s_inundation.specific_hazard: Rapid olfactory fatigue - cannot rely on smell for warning

combustion_products.source: Underground fire, diesel engine exhaust, blasting fumes
combustion_products.immediate_danger: CO causes rapid incapacitation, NO2 causes delayed pulmonary edema

detection.monitoring: Continuous gas monitoring throughout mine with surface display and alarm
detection.personal_monitors: Multi-gas detector on all underground personnel (O2, CO, H2S, CH4)
detection.alarm_response: Immediate evacuation on gas alarm, do not investigate without SCBA

evacuation.self_rescuer: Deploy self-rescuer immediately upon gas detection, do not remove until in fresh air
evacuation.route: Primary escape route to fresh air intake or surface, DO NOT travel through contaminated air
evacuation.assembly: Assembly point at surface, headcount within 15 minutes

containment.ventilation_adjustment: Increase fresh air to affected area, consider ventilation reversal for fire-related gas
containment.sealing: Seal affected area if gas source cannot be controlled, install monitoring on seals
containment.gas_drainage: Activate methane drainage system to reduce gas concentration

reentry.conditions: Gas levels below action thresholds for minimum 4 consecutive hours
reentry.testing: Atmospheric testing at multiple heights before any personnel entry
reentry.equipment: SCBA required for all re-entry personnel, continuous gas monitoring
reentry.authorization: Only by mine manager after qualified person certification of safe conditions

team_composition.minimum_team_size: 6 persons per team (4 rescuers + 2 surface support)
team_composition.team_leader: Minimum 5 years rescue experience, certified mine rescue team leader
team_composition.composition: Mix of experienced miners, engineers, and first-aid qualified personnel
team_composition.ratio: Minimum 2 teams on standby for any mine with >50 underground personnel

breathing_apparatus.type: Closed-circuit breathing apparatus (CCBA) per MSHA Part 75 or equivalent
breathing_apparatus.quantity: One per rescuer, plus 50% spare units at base
breathing_apparatus.maintenance: Post-use overhaul, weekly inspection, annual hydrostatic test of cylinders

communication.primary: Leaky feeder radio integrated with mine communication system
communication.tertiary: Messenger system using pre-installed communication wires

detection_instruments.multi_gas_detector: O2, LEL, CO, H2S - calibrated before each deployment
detection_instruments.thermal_imaging_camera: For locating victims in smoke or darkness
detection_instruments.acoustic_listening_device: For locating trapped persons through rubble

rescue_tools.hydraulic_cutting_spreading: Holmatro or equivalent hydraulic rescue tools
rescue_tools.pneumatic_cribbing: Temporary support systems for unstable areas
rescue_tools.winches: Hand and powered winches for victim extraction
rescue_tools.stretchers: Sked stretcher, Stokes basket, Neil Robertson stretcher for confined spaces

training.frequency: Minimum 4 hours training per month, 2 full-scale drills per quarter
training.external_drills: Participation in inter-mine rescue competition/drill annually

response_time.notification: Rescue team notified within 5 minutes of emergency declaration
response_time.mobilization: Team assembled and equipped within 30 minutes of notification
response_time.underground_entry: Team underground and operating within 60 minutes of emergency
response_time.sustained_operations: 12-hour shifts with minimum 12-hour rest between shifts, rotation of teams

reportable_incidents.reporting_timeframe: Immediately to MSHA (within 15 minutes) and regulatory authority
reportable_incidents.requirements: Site immediately preserved for investigation unless preservation would endanger persons
examples: Death from any cause while underground or at mine site
Death within 30 days of mine-related injury or illness

reportable_incidents.reporting_timeframe: Immediately to MSHA and regulatory authority

reportable_incidents.requirements: Written notification within 24 hours, full investigation within 30 days
examples: Hospitalization of one or more persons
Loss of consciousness due to gas exposure

reportable_incidents.reporting_timeframe: Immediately for misfires and premature detonations
Within 24 hours for significant events, immediately if personnel endangered
Immediately for underground fires, within 24 hours for surface
examples: Any underground fire regardless of size

reportable_incidents.reporting_timeframe: Within 24 hours to environmental regulatory authority

examples: Equipment failure with potential for injury
reportable_incidents.purpose: Learning and prevention, non-punitive reporting culture encouraged

immediate_response: Secure the scene and render it safe
Provide first aid and medical treatment to injured persons
Notify management and regulatory authority per reportable thresholds
Preserve evidence (photographs, video, physical evidence, electronic data)
Establish cordon and control access to incident scene

composition: Investigation leader (safety professional or senior engineer)
Site supervisor familiar with the area and operations
Technical specialist as required (geologist, engineer, metallurgist)
investigation_team.timeline: Team assembled within 4 hours for significant incidents, within 24 hours for all others
investigation_team.independence: Investigation team must not include persons with direct management responsibility for the area

evidence_collection.physical_evidence: Photograph, sketch, and collect physical samples. Tag and secure all evidence.
evidence_collection.witness_statements: Interview all witnesses within 24 hours. Separate interviews. Record with consent.
evidence_collection.electronic_data: Download and secure: CCTV footage, equipment data recorders, gas monitoring data, personnel tracking data, communication logs
evidence_collection.environmental_conditions: Weather data, gas levels, ground conditions, lighting levels at time of incident
evidence_collection.procedural_documents: Safe work procedures, training records, inspection reports, maintenance records relevant to the area

investigation_phases.phase_1_data_collection: Gather all facts, evidence, and witness accounts (Days 1-7)
investigation_phases.phase_2_analysis: Determine immediate causes and contributing factors (Days 7-14)
investigation_phases.phase_3_root_cause: Identify systemic root causes using structured methodology (Days 14-21)
investigation_phases.phase_4_recommendations: Develop corrective actions to prevent recurrence (Days 21-30)
investigation_phases.phase_5_report: Complete investigation report with findings, causes, and recommendations (Day 30)

methodologies.description: Iterative questioning technique to peel back layers of symptoms to root causes
methodologies.application: Simple to moderate incidents, single causal chain
methodologies.process: Start with problem statement, ask 'Why?' five times or until systemic cause identified

methodologies.description: Top-down deductive analysis of all possible causes of an undesired event
methodologies.application: Complex incidents with multiple potential causes

methodologies.description: Visual risk assessment linking threats, preventive barriers, event, mitigative barriers, consequences
Systematic root cause analysis methodology using causal factor charting and root cause trees
methodologies.strengths: Distinguishes between human error, equipment failure, and management system weaknesses

methodologies.description: Multi-level sociotechnical analysis of accident causation across organizational hierarchy
methodologies.application: Systemic failures involving multiple organizational levels

common_root_causes_in_mining: Inadequate risk assessment or no risk assessment for the task
Failure to follow established safe work procedures
Poor housekeeping or housekeeping standards not enforced
Failure to maintain equipment or safety-critical systems
Inadequate hazard identification during task planning
Communication breakdowns between shifts or departments
Design deficiencies in equipment, infrastructure, or procedures
Failure to learn from previous incidents or near misses
Poor safety culture and reporting environment

short_term_actions.responsible: Action owner assigned at investigation close-out
short_term_actions.verification: Documented verification with evidence of completion

medium_term_actions.verification: Monthly progress review, completion verified by safety team

tracking_system.platform: Dedicated incident management software (e.g., Enablon, Intelex, Cority)
tracking_system.escalation: Overdue actions escalated: 1 day overdue to supervisor, 7 days to department head, 14 days to mine manager, 30 days to corporate safety
tracking_system.reporting: Weekly corrective action status report to management, monthly to board/safety committee

effectiveness_verification.method: Re-inspection of area/process after action implementation, monitoring of recurrence
metrics: Corrective action completion rate (target: 100% on time)
Time to implementation vs planned time

induction_program.duration: Minimum 2 days (16 hours) for new underground workers, 1 day (8 hours) for surface-only

delivery.classroom: Qualified trainer, minimum 3 years mining experience
delivery.certification: Induction certificate valid for 2 years, refresher required

site_specific_additions: Mine-specific emergency procedures and contact numbers

refresher_training.frequency: Annual refresher for all workers, quarterly for high-risk activities

records.tracking: Learning management system tracks all training records, expiry dates, and compliance status
records.non_compliance: Workers with expired training cannot perform the relevant task until retrained

specialized_certifications.issuing_body: Council of Certified Mine Safety Professionals (CCMSP)
specialized_certifications.requirements: 5 years mining experience, bachelor's degree, pass examination
Supervised blasting experience, formal training course, practical assessment, written examination
Degree in mining/geological engineering or equivalent experience, mine-specific competency assessment
specialized_certifications.responsibilities: Examine ground conditions, authorize support, assess stability

specialized_certifications.requirements: Training in ventilation engineering, gas detection, atmospheric monitoring
specialized_certifications.responsibilities: Monitor and manage mine atmosphere, authorize re-entry after gas events

specialized_certifications.issuing_body: MSHA or State mine rescue organization
specialized_certifications.requirements: Physical fitness, training hours, breathing apparatus proficiency, first aid
40-hour HAZWOPER training + 8-hour annual refresher, practical exercise
specialized_certifications.scope: Emergency response to hazardous material releases

specialized_certifications.requirements: Training in atmospheric monitoring, rescue procedures, communication, ventilation
specialized_certifications.scope: Entry into confined spaces per permit system

specialized_certifications.issuing_body: American Red Cross, St John Ambulance, or equivalent
specialized_certifications.requirements: Practical course, minimum 8 hours initial, 4 hours refresher
specialized_certifications.minimum_coverage: Minimum 1 first-aider per 25 workers at any location on site

specialized_certifications.requirements: Standard 11 generic induction, site-specific induction, task-specific training
specialized_certifications.scope: Mandatory for all mine workers in Australian mining jurisdictions

evacuation_drills.frequency: Quarterly full mine evacuation drill, monthly table-top exercise
objectives: All personnel reach surface or refuge within 30 minutes
Headcount completed within 15 minutes of surface arrival
evacuation_drills.evaluation: Time to evacuate, percentage of personnel accounted for, communication effectiveness
evacuation_drills.documentation: Drill report filed within 24 hours, deficiencies assigned corrective actions

self_rescuer_drills.requirements: Each worker deploys self-rescuer in <30 seconds, demonstrates correct procedure
self_rescuer_drills.recording: Time recorded for each worker, remedial training for any exceeding 30 seconds

scenarios: Workshop fire with chemical storage nearby
fire_response_drills.involvement: Mine rescue team + all on-shift personnel, coordination with external fire services annually

flood_response_drills.frequency: Annual comprehensive drill, triggered drill after heavy rainfall events

refuge_chamber_drills.frequency: Semi-annual full drill with timed entry
refuge_chamber_drills.requirements: All personnel from furthest point enter chamber within rated travel time, door sealed, communication established with surface
refuge_chamber_drills.assessment: Air supply activation, communication check, personnel accounting

applicable_subchapters.subchapter: Part 50 - Reporting and Investigation of Accidents
key_requirements: Immediate notification of fatalities and entrapments
24-hour notification of hospitalization, loss of consciousness
Investigation and report submission within timeframes

applicable_subchapters.subchapter: Part 56 - Safety and Health Standards - Surface Metal and Nonmetal Mines
key_requirements: Health standards - dust, noise, radiation (Subpart D/SS/T)

applicable_subchapters.subchapter: Part 57 - Safety and Health Standards - Underground Metal and Nonmetal Mines

key_requirements: Action level: 85 dBA TWA triggers hearing conservation program
DPM exposure limit: 160 μg/m³ total carbon (TC) TWA

applicable_subchapters.subchapter: Part 72 - Air Quality, Social Contact, and Roof Ground Control (Coal)
Part 75 - Mandatory Safety Standards - Underground Coal Mines
key_requirements: Emergency plans and refuge alternatives (Subpart K)
New miner training: minimum 40 hours (surface) / 40 hours (underground)
Newly hired experienced miner: minimum 8 hours

inspection_schedule.mandatory_inspections: MSHA conducts minimum 2 inspections per year for underground coal mines, 2 per year for surface metal/nonmetal, 1 per year for all other mines
inspection_schedule.cooperation: Mine operators must cooperate with inspectors, provide access to all areas, produce requested records

types.104_a: Citation - violation of mandatory standard, specify abatement date
types.104_b: Order of withdrawal - imminent danger, requires immediate withdrawal
types.104_k: Closure order - pattern of violations, mine closure until violations corrected

international_standards.title: Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems - Requirements
international_standards.scope: Framework for managing OH&S risks and opportunities
key_elements: Operation (operational planning and control, emergency preparedness)
Performance evaluation (monitoring, internal audit, management review)
international_standards.certification: Third-party certification available, often required by major mining companies

international_standards.title: Safety and Health in Mines Convention, 1995
international_standards.scope: International labor standard for mining safety
key_provisions: Employer responsibility for safety and health
international_standards.ratification: Adopted by 30+ countries, provides international minimum standard

international_standards.title: International Cyanide Management Code
international_standards.scope: Safe manufacture, transport, storage, and use of cyanide in gold production
international_standards.auditing: Independent third-party audit required for code signatories

international_standards.title: Environmental Management Systems - Requirements
international_standards.scope: Environmental management framework for mining operations
international_standards.relevance: Often integrated with ISO 45001 for combined HSE management system

international_standards.title: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table
international_standards.scope: Design requirements for mobile equipment safety in mining

international_standards.title: Mining - Mobile Machines Working Underground - Machine Safety
international_standards.scope: Safety requirements for mobile machines operating in underground mines

international_standards.title: Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems
international_standards.scope: Australian/New Zealand standard, still referenced in some contracts

international_standards.title: Workplace Electrical Safety
international_standards.scope: Canadian standard for electrical safety in workplace, applicable to mining

items: Safety policy signed by CEO/Managing Director and displayed
Safety objectives and targets set annually, measurable
Safety as agenda item at every board/management meeting
Management visible in safety activities (walkthroughs, audits, incident reviews)
Safety performance linked to management compensation
Adequate budget allocated for safety improvements
Safety committee meets monthly with worker representatives
Risk register maintained and reviewed quarterly
Formal risk assessments completed for all high-risk activities
Change management process implemented for all significant changes
Job Safety Analyses (JSAs) completed for all routine and non-routine tasks
Risk assessment training for all supervisors and engineers
Bow-tie analysis completed for top 10 risks
Risk register reviewed after every incident or near miss
All applicable regulations identified and documented
Legal requirements register maintained and current
Regulatory authority notifications completed within required timeframes
All required licenses and permits current
Mine plan approved and current
Environmental approvals current and conditions met
Workers' compensation insurance current
Emergency response plan documented and accessible
Emergency drills conducted per schedule (quarterly evacuation, etc.)
Rescue teams adequately trained and equipped
Refuge chambers inspected and functional
Emergency communication systems tested regularly
External emergency services familiar with mine layout
Evacuation routes signposted and unobstructed
Induction program covers all required topics
Refresher training up to date for all workers
Specialized certifications current for all applicable roles
Competency assessments conducted for safety-critical tasks
Training records maintained and accessible
Contractor training requirements defined and verified
New equipment/process training completed before implementation
Hazard reporting system non-punitive and accessible
Regular hazard inspections conducted (daily supervisor, weekly management)
Engineering controls implemented per hierarchy of controls
Contractor safety management system in place
Chemical inventory and SDS library maintained
Dust and noise monitoring program operational
Vehicle interaction management plan implemented
Incident reporting system functional and user-friendly
Investigation completed within required timeframes
Root cause analysis performed for all significant incidents
Corrective actions tracked to completion
Incident learnings shared with all workforce
Regulatory reporting completed within required timeframes
Near miss reporting encouraged and analyzed for trends
Maintenance management system in place and utilized
Safety-critical equipment on planned maintenance schedule
Pre-start safety checks completed for mobile equipment
Guarding in place on all moving parts and pinch points
Fire protection systems tested and maintained
Electrical installations comply with relevant standards
Pressure systems tested per regulatory requirements
Occupational health program in place (spirometry, audiometry, biological monitoring)
Dust monitoring program meets regulatory requirements
Noise monitoring program meets regulatory requirements
Heat stress management program for hot environments
Health surveillance records maintained
Cafeteria/food safety meets health department requirements
Sanitary facilities adequate and maintained
Contractor pre-qualification process in place
Contractor safety requirements documented in contracts
Contractor induction completed before site access
Contractor safety performance monitored and reported
Contractor incident reporting requirements defined
Contractor equipment meets site standards
Contractor competency verification completed

leading_indicators.metric: Safety training hours per worker per month
Hazard reports submitted per worker per month
Safety observations completed per supervisor per week

leading_indicators.target: Increasing trend indicates improving safety culture

lagging_indicators.metric: Days Lost / Disabling Injury Frequency Rate

lagging_indicators.formula: Number of environmental exceedances or spills per quarter
